parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: Liability language most likely sits immediately after the all-caps warranty disclaimer block (sec-p0109/p0112/p0116) or in Article X / General Provisions. Check for a one-sided cap favouring Licensor, absence of carve-outs (confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence/willful misconduct), and whether consequential-damages exclusion is mutual. Do not double-flag the warranty disclaimer itself, which is handled under WARRANTY.

No indemnity heading is visible in the outline; scan Article X, Article XXIV and General Provisions for a Licensor IP-infringement indemnity and any reverse indemnity imposed on us as Licensee. If only a Licensee-side indemnity exists, treat as deviation; if nothing exists, treat as missing.

Article II is expressly 'LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS' and is the most likely home for restrictions on our business, FIELD OF USE limits, or a bar on competing/self-built platforms; also check the non-solicitation article (sec-p0123) for bolted-on competitive restraints.

The defined terms 'Right of First Refusal' and 'FIELD OF USE' signal a possible exclusivity or ROFR obligation binding us; trace the definition in Article I to its operative use (likely Article II or the fee/Article VIII block) and assess whether we are barred from sourcing alternative FX platforms.

The tiered per-trade pricing schedule is where any most-favoured-customer language would appear. No MFN heading is apparent; only flag if an operative clause requires us to extend our best terms to Licensor. An MFN running in our favour is welcome and should not be redlined.

Article X is headed 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION' — the operative non-solicit sits here. Check mutuality, duration (accept ~12 months, fallback 24), scope (employees actually involved in the engagement) and whether a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out exists.

'Initial Period' is a defined term, so term/termination mechanics exist somewhere; look in the later articles (XXIV and General Provisions) and in the fee/Article VIII block. Assess whether we may terminate on notice without penalty and whether Licensor holds a broader or at-will termination right or a revocable-licence trigger.

Check the 'Initial Period' definition and the termination article for automatic renewal, the length of the notice window for non-renewal, and any uncapped renewal price uplift. A missing uplift cap alone is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Governing law, venue and any dispute-resolution/arbitration provision will sit in the GENERAL PROVISIONS block. New York is likely given the 575 Madison Avenue address and is an accepted law; flag only foreign law, foreign-seated arbitration, or an inconvenient exclusive venue.

Assignment/successors language belongs in GENERAL PROVISIONS. Confirm we may assign to AFFILIATEs (defined in Article I) and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that Licensor cannot terminate on our change of control.

Article I defines DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, MORAL RIGHTS, LICENSED TECHNOLOGY and PLATFORM SOFTWARE; Article II will contain the operative ownership/assignment language. Watch for any assignment to Licensor of our data, feedback, configurations or customer/trade data, and for feedback-ownership grabs in the confidentiality article.

Article II is the grant clause. Test whether the licence extends to our AFFILIATEs and contractors, whether the FIELD OF USE definition is unduly narrow, and whether the grant is revocable at will or terminable on unilateral Licensor notice.

Any audit/verification right over our usage or trade volumes would sit with the licence restrictions (Article II) or alongside the tiered volume pricing/reporting obligations. Check frequency, notice, business-hours limits, confidentiality and who bears cost.

Look in the fee/Supplemental Payments material for late-payment interest, stipulated damages or accelerated-fee penalties payable by us. Ordinary commercial interest on late payment is not an LD; only genuine penalty or acceleration language is a deviation.

Article VIX contains an all-caps WARRANTY DISCLAIMER expressly disclaiming merchantability, non-infringement and fitness for purpose, and stating that defects in the software/DOCUMENTATION may not be corrected. Expect a deviation: there appears to be no affirmative performance warranty or repair/replace/refund remedy for us.

No insurance heading appears anywhere in the outline; confirm by scanning GENERAL PROVISIONS. If absent, treat as missing and request standard coverages (commercial general liability, tech E&O/cyber) given Licensor hosts the Platform and handles our trade data.

The volume-tiered per-trade rates and the defined 'Supplemental Payments' / 'Market Day' terms suggest a minimum-volume or minimum-fee construct. Determine whether we owe fees regardless of actual volume and whether any shortfall triggers a take-or-pay with no exit.

No exit/transition heading is visible; check the termination consequences (likely Article XXIV) and the confidentiality article for return-or-destroy language. Note that a confidentiality return-of-materials clause running against us is not a substitute for return of our own trade data plus transition assistance.
